ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The bar chart lists four indicators: “freshwater resources, scientific and technological strength, population, area”; the legend shows that hollow bars are the east and solid bars are the west. In the figure, the east has relatively high shares of area and freshwater resources; area accounts for about around 70%, and freshwater resources are close to 90%; the west has very high shares in scientific and technological strength and population, with scientific and technological strength close to 90% and population about around 80%, while the shares of area and freshwater resources are relatively low. Reasoning: This pattern of two major economic zones, “the east has vast area and many resources, while the west has concentrated population and science and technology,” matches the east-west differences of Russia. Russia has a high latitude; agriculture is mainly distributed in the warmer European part and southern regions, while the vast northern and eastern regions are limited in agricultural development because of cold climate and insufficient heat. Therefore, the primary factor determining the agricultural regional type of this country is not area, population, or scientific and technological strength, but climatic conditions.
